findings.description: The Lambda function embeds a literal AWS access key ID (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE) and secret access key in its environment variables. These values are stored in plaintext in Terraform state and the function configuration, are readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and cannot be rotated without a redeploy. Secrets should be supplied via Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store and referenced at runtime.

The function is configured with runtime "nodejs12.x", which is long past end of life and no longer receives security patches. Running an unsupported runtime means known vulnerabilities in the language and standard library remain unpatched in this execution environment.

findings.issue_category: overly permissive role / no scoped permissions
findings.description: The role's trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume it, but the configuration defines no attached or inline permission policy. In this state the role carries no least-privilege boundary; if permissions are later granted broadly (or via an account-level policy), the function's embedded long-lived credentials and the role's permissions combine to form a privilege-escalation path. Review and scope any policy attached to this role.
